newsitem.title: CHINA: Shanghai copper ends up on Chile worker strike.
newsitem.headline: Shanghai copper ends up on Chile worker strike.

text.p: Shanghai copper futures ended up on Wednesday because of a strike by workers at a copper mine in Chile, traders said.
Workers at Chile's state-owned Codelco's Salvador copper mine voted to begin an indefinite strike as of August 31 to demand higher wages, traders said.
Traders said the strike would trigger expectations of spot tightness, which would push up futures prices.
The most active December 1996 contract ended at an intra- day high of 20,500 yuan ($2,468) per tonne, up 250 yuan. It opened at a low of 20,250.
September rose 30 to 21,050 yuan, October 100 to 20,700, November 170 to 20,500, the January 1997 contract 230 to 20,430, February 170 to 20,420 and March 150 to 20,500.
Combined volume rose to 12,310 tonnes from 4,695.
Copper opened little changed and rose steadily, boosted by news of the strike, for the most of the session.
The news boosted confidence of long position holders, but later-maturing contracts met resistance at around 20,500 yuan, traders said.
"The strike was responsible for today's rises," one trader said. "But copper met strong resistance, with investors waiting to see movements on the London Metal Exchange."
Some traders said the impact of the strike news would be limited due to poor mid- and long-term fundamentals.
"Copper could rebound a little thanks to positive news, but its downward trend in the mid- and long-term will not change," a second trader said.
Aluminium ended up. September rose 120 to 14,390 yuan and October 70 to 14,250. Combined volume fell to 380 tonnes from 480. ($1=8.3087 yuan)
